output.summary: The yield decline is real: gauge R&R, the CMM program and reject criteria are stable, and Halvard's receiving PPM rose. The new-operator cohort is ruled out, because new and experienced operators reject at about the same rate and yield was already falling before they ran alone. The scrap-tag timestamps record when tags were written, so they say nothing about fatigue. Corvane hardness spread and spindle wear are fully confounded. Both began in August, the high-spread lots ran later, and no Corvane-on-serviced-spindle or Tamsworth-on-worn-spindle data exists. The attribution is therefore open. Backlog pressure demonstrably deferred the service. The best next step is the staggered service with Tamsworth trial lots and logging, plus the Line 6 CMM data and the cycle-counter match. Reverting shifts, blaming steel, disciplining operators or sampling inspection would be premature or harmful.
